history.llm_reasoning: Round 1 (all defaults) scored 0.6269 best / 0.6225 final, statistically indistinguishable from the 0.6198 +/- 0.0110 baseline given the 0.0219 noise threshold, so it serves as characterization rather than improvement. The only triggered flag is D4 Localization Bottleneck: mAP50=0.9495 vs mAP50-95=0.6225, gap 0.3270 above the 0.3261 threshold. Every class has AP50 >= 0.927 with P/R in the 0.87-0.93 range, so detection and classification are effectively solved and 100% of the remaining headroom sits in box regression tightness at high IoU. D5 did not trigger (gap 0.176 < 0.227); yellow light is weakest at 0.5225 but its AP50 is 0.9358, confirming it is the same localization deficit amplified by the smallest sample count (n=48), not a recognition failure, so a global localization fix should lift it most. D1/D2/D3 all clear: val loss 2.749 vs train 2.448 with no rising tail means no overfitting, and best epoch 93 of 100 with plateau onset only at epoch 72 means the model was still improving under linear decay to 0.000199. Therefore regularization and schedule-shortening levers address problems this run does not have and would waste budget. I make two coordinated edits on one mechanism: box 7.5 -> 10.0 shifts loss weight from saturated classification into IoU/DFL regression, the direct lever for D4; mosaic 1.0 -> 0.7 reduces the tiling that downscales already-small traffic lights and clips boxes at tile boundaries, restoring full-resolution unclipped box supervision on ~30% of batches, which is affordable precisely because D3 shows spare overfitting headroom. lr0, weight_decay and hsv_v are frozen since the LR schedule demonstrably worked and hsv_v is photometric and cannot affect box tightness, keeping the result attributable. Budget note: at round 1 of 10 with 9 remaining and a 0.0219 noise floor, single-variable 10% nudges are unmeasurable, so I pair two mutually reinforcing levers to produce a readable signal and falsify or confirm the localization hypothesis in one round, leaving 8 rounds to pivot to LR and class-balance territory if it fails, with the final 2-3 reserved for consolidating the best point.

history.llm_reasoning: Round 2 regressed to 0.5993, ~0.028 below the Round-1 baseline of 0.6269 — beyond the 0.0219 noise threshold, so it is a genuine regression and that direction should be abandoned. The effective LR trace (end 0.000199 = lr0*0.0199 at epoch 99) shows lr0 was still 0.01, so the damage came from the regularization/augmentation/box group. I therefore revert to the Round-1 configuration as the base. Diagnostics point clearly at localization: D4 missed its flag by only 0.005 (gap 0.3214 vs 0.3261) while mAP50 is already 0.9206 against mAP50-95 of 0.5992 — detection at IoU 0.5 is essentially solved, so all remaining headroom is in tighter box regression. This pairs naturally with D1+D2 (mAP plateaus at epoch 45 while train loss keeps falling 9.56 -> 2.95): the second half of training keeps reducing loss without converting it into mAP, consistent with easy classification gains continuing while regression quality stalls. D3 is NOT triggered (val loss never turns up), so this is not an overfitting/regularization problem and I leave weight_decay, mosaic and hsv_v at their Round-1 values to keep the experiment attributable. D5 is NOT triggered (gap 0.196 < 0.227); yellow light remains weakest (AP 0.479, R 0.729) but with n=48 it is the noisiest figure in the report, and its own AP50-to-AP50-95 gap of 0.391 is the largest of the three classes, meaning a localization fix should help it most anyway. So I raise box 7.5 -> 10.0 to re-weight the regression term (a +33% step, still far from the 15.0 ceiling so there is room to push again if it works) and lower lr0 0.01 -> 0.008 so the late linear-decay phase refines box coordinates instead of jittering them. With 8 rounds left I can afford this one clean two-lever test: if it clears 0.6269 the localization hypothesis is confirmed and I escalate box further; if not, I pivot to the augmentation group with the remaining budget.

history.llm_reasoning: mAP50 is saturated at 0.9486 while mAP50-95 is 0.6250; the D4 gap (0.3236) sits essentially on its 0.3261 threshold, and every class shows the same pattern (yellow: AP50 0.959 vs AP50-95 0.519 despite P=0.953/R=0.938). history.llm_reasoning: Rounds 1, 3 and 4 (0.6269 / 0.6250 / 0.6206) all fall within the 0.0219 noise threshold of each other and of the 0.6198 baseline, so lr0 (0.008-0.010) and box (7.5-10.0) are demonstrated dead axes; D4 NOT TRIGGERED (gap 0.3138 < 0.3261) independently confirms there is no localization bottleneck to justify further box tuning. Round 2 is the only signal-level result (-0.0276) and isolates mosaic=0.7 as harmful, since Round 3 retained box=10.0 with mosaic=1.0 and lost nothing; mosaic therefore stays pinned at 1.0. The decisive evidence this round is D1+D2 TRIGGERED with D3 NOT TRIGGERED: mAP plateaus at epoch 51 of 100 while train loss continues falling 9.68->2.98, yet val loss does NOT rise (3.2567 end). That pattern is not memorization of noise, it is exhaustion of training-data variety - the second half of the epoch budget is spent on inputs the network has already fully absorbed. The remedy is input-space variety, not a smaller step size or a reweighted loss. hsv_v is the only hyperparameter untouched across all four rounds (fixed at 0.4) and is the one physically matched to this dataset: traffic lights are self-luminous emitters imaged under day/night, glare, backlight and exposure variation, so value-channel jitter directly synthesizes the missing variety. Per-class data agrees: yellow light has P=0.9013 but R=0.7500 on only n=48 - high confidence on what it finds, missing a quarter of instances - a coverage deficit that brightness augmentation directly expands. With 6 rounds left I am making one large, clean move (hsv_v 0.4 -> 0.7, +75%) rather than a timid or multi-parameter one: large enough that a real effect clears the 0.0219 threshold instead of vanishing into it, and single-axis so the result is unambiguously attributable. This keeps the remaining budget interpretable - if it helps, push further and then tune weight_decay (the other never-probed axis) on top; if not, the last cheap axis is eliminated and I revert to Round 1 and spend the remainder on weight_decay.
history.llm_base_rationale: Round 1 is the historical best (0.6269) and its lr0=0.01 / mosaic=1.0 / box=7.5 settings survived three subsequent attempts to beat them. history.llm_reasoning: Five rounds have yielded a 0.6206-0.6269 spread against a 0.0219 noise threshold, i.e. no signal. history.llm_reasoning: All six rounds fall within the 0.0219 noise threshold (spread 0.0063), so five rounds of small single-parameter probes have yielded zero statistically real signal; with 4 rounds left I need a change large enough to clear noise. Diagnostics localize the headroom precisely: D1+D2 triggered (mAP plateaus at epoch 54/100 while train loss keeps falling 8.42->2.53), D3 NOT triggered (val loss not rising), so the wasted second half is not overfitting and the regularization budget is over-spent. D4 misses by only 0.0095 (gap 0.3166 vs 0.3261) with mAP50=0.9392 against mAP50-95=0.6226 - detection is solved, box-corner precision is the entire remaining loss. Yellow light proves it: AP50=0.9406 (on par with red/green) but AP50-95=0.5093, i.e. found reliably, bounded sloppily; that is also why D5 stays untriggered. The standard response is to raise box, but box=10.0 was tested three times (R2 0.5993, R3 0.6250, R4 0.6206) and never beat box=7.5 (R1 0.6269, R5 0.6266) - that direction is explored and dead. The downward direction is untouched and mechanistically motivated: CIoU (box) optimizes whole-box overlap, which mAP50=0.94 shows is already saturated, while DFL (fixed at 1.5) optimizes the coordinate distribution that governs IoU 0.75-0.95 where the 0.32 gap lives. Cutting box 7.5->5.0 raises DFL's relative share of regression gradient by ~50%. I pair this with weight_decay 0.0005->0.0002, licensed by D3's absence of overfitting, so the head can keep sharpening through the epoch 54-90 dead zone instead of being pulled toward small weights. Both changes push the same direction (stop constraining the fine-grained fit), so the result is interpretable either way. Holding mosaic=1.0 (R2 shows heavy mosaic is load-bearing), hsv_v=0.4 (0.7 was neutral at 0.6266, not the lever), and lr0=0.01 (already at range max; 0.008 gave no benefit).

history.llm_reasoning: Rounds 1-7 are all within the 0.0219 noise threshold of each other and of the 0.6198 baseline; six single-variable nudges around the default point have yielded no real gain, so with 3 rounds remaining I take one decisive step into untested space instead of another noise sample. The only trend with support is box gain: box=7.5 averaged 0.6254 across three runs, box=10.0 averaged 0.6150 across three runs, monotone in all comparisons. Raising box has now failed three times, and box<7.5 has never been tested. D4 (localization bottleneck, gap 0.332) is triggered and is concentrated in yellow light (AP50=0.9255 vs AP50-95=0.5024, n=48, small objects) - but the naive D4 response of raising box gain is exactly what Rounds 2/3/4 tried and it lost every time. Mechanistically, over-weighting the box (CIoU) term for small objects starves the DFL branch, which is what actually sharpens high-IoU box distributions; lowering box to 5.0 raises the relative weight of dfl/cls and is the untested lever aimed directly at the high-IoU deficit. D1+D2 (plateau at epoch 67 with train loss still falling, D3 not triggered) says this is a loss-weighting/objective-misalignment problem, not overfitting and not an LR problem - consistent with Round 6 (wd=0.0015, 0.6226) and Round 3 (lr0=0.008, 0.6250) both being dead ends. I therefore change only box, holding mosaic=1.0 (mosaic=0.7 gave the single worst run, 0.5993, the only result clearly outside noise), hsv_v=0.4 (0.4 vs 0.7 gave 0.6269 vs 0.6266, provably neutral), lr0=0.01 and wd=0.0005 at their best-known values. A single-variable large step keeps the result attributable: if box=5.0 gains, Round 9 pushes to ~3.5 and Round 10 consolidates; if it loses, box is settled at 7.5 and the remaining rounds revert to Round 1 and probe the untested mosaic 0.85-0.95 window.

history.llm_reasoning: Seven rounds of single-variable probing produced no change exceeding the 0.0219 noise threshold, so incremental testing is not viable in the 2 remaining rounds; a larger combined step is needed. Signals: box weight is the only monotone axis (10 -> hurt, 7.5 -> baseline, 5.0 -> best 0.6293) and D4 NOT TRIGGERED (gap 0.3238 < 0.3261) confirms localization is not the bottleneck, so loss weight on box regression is wasted -- push to 4.0. weight_decay=0.0005 is a sharp optimum (0.0002 -> 0.6117, 0.0015 -> 0.6226), so freeze it. mosaic must stay 1.0 (0.7 -> 0.5993, the only clearly-bad result). hsv_v is a free axis (0.4 vs 0.7 indistinguishable at box=7.5), so spend it on the real problem: D1+D2 TRIGGERED with plateau at epoch 34 while train loss falls 7.77->2.17 and D3 shows no val-loss rise -- the model exhausts input diversity then memorizes, which calls for more photometric variation rather than more regularization (already disproven by R6/R7). Yellow light (AP50=0.9536 but AP50-95=0.5399, n=48) is the class most likely to benefit from brightness diversity. Hence box 5.0->4.0 plus hsv_v 0.4->0.6 in one decisive move, holding lr0, weight_decay and mosaic at verified optima. Round 10 is reserved to either extend this direction or fall back to the R8 configuration.

With one round of budget left, I extend that trend with a single controlled step to box=4.0 rather than re-running the known best (which cannot raise the ceiling) or making a large multi-parameter jump (the only moves that have demonstrably lost performance). Lowering box shifts loss weight from regression toward classification/DFL, consistent with mAP50 already at 0.9416 and D4 sitting just under its threshold: the remaining error is ranking and fine localization quality, not box detection. All other parameters are held at the historical-best values.

Building on it lets the final round add a fourth, directly comparable point to the only monotonic trend in the study while changing exactly one variable, minimizing the risk seen in R2 and R7 where simultaneous changes moved away from this neighbourhood and lost 0.012-0.030 mAP.

history.llm_reasoning: Final round of a fixed 10-round budget; no further evaluation is possible, so the proposal must be the deployable optimum rather than an exploratory probe. Round 10 (this run) is the campaign best at 0.6320. The single reliable signal across all rounds is a monotone four-point trend in box loss weight with all else held at lr0=0.01/wd=0.0005/mosaic=1.0/hsv_v=0.4: box=10.0->0.6206, 7.5->0.6269, 5.0->0.6293, 4.0->0.6320. This is consistent with D4 NOT TRIGGERED (gap 0.3042 < 0.3261 threshold) — localization was never the bottleneck, so down-weighting box loss reallocates capacity to classification/DFL without harming regression (final mAP50 still 0.9343). I decline to extrapolate to box=3.0 because the marginal gain is decaying (+0.0063, +0.0024, +0.0027) and round 9 showed box=4.0 is fragile to co-perturbation (box=4.0 + hsv_v=0.6 -> 0.6222), and an unverified point should not be shipped. All other parameters are held at values whose alternatives were tested and lost: lr0=0.008 -> 0.6250; mosaic=0.7 -> 0.5993 (worst run of the campaign); wd=0.0015 -> 0.6226 and wd=0.0002 -> 0.6117, consistent with D3 NOT TRIGGERED (val loss fell 12.52->2.20 with no tail rise, so there is no overfitting to regularize); hsv_v=0.7/0.65/0.6 were neutral-to-negative. Caveat: D1 and D2 both TRIGGERED here (plateau from epoch 57 of 100 while train loss kept falling 8.12->2.04), indicating the binding constraint is the epoch schedule and data, not these five knobs — and the total gain over baseline (+0.0122) is below the 0.0219 noise threshold, so no statistically significant improvement can be claimed from single-seed runs. The box trend is credible only because it is monotone across four points. Recommend 5-seed confirmation of this configuration before treating it as a real improvement.
history.llm_base_rationale: Round 10 is the highest-scoring configuration observed (0.6320) and sits at the endpoint of the only monotone, single-variable trend identified in the campaign (decreasing box weight). With zero rounds remaining, the expected-value-maximizing move is to consolidate on this verified point rather than gamble the final proposal on an untested extrapolation such as box=3.0.

history.llm_reasoning: Round 11 duplicated Round 10 and reproduced 0.6320, confirming the optimum is stable but yielding no new search information. Across all 11 rounds the only clean monotonic trend is box weight at fixed lr0=0.01/wd=0.0005/mosaic=1.0/hsv_v=0.4: box=10.0 -> 0.6206, 7.5 -> 0.6269, 5.0 -> 0.6293, 4.0 -> 0.6320. All other axes are tested and rejected: mosaic=0.7 collapses to 0.5993, hsv_v=0.6-0.7 is neutral-to-harmful (Round 9's box=4.0+hsv_v=0.6 gives 0.6222 vs 0.6320 with hsv_v=0.4), wd=0.0015 -> 0.6226 and wd=0.0002 -> 0.6117 both lose to 0.0005, and lr0=0.008 shows no benefit. D3 NOT TRIGGERED (val loss 12.52 -> 2.20, still decreasing) rules out overfitting, so raising weight_decay or cutting augmentation is unjustified. D4 NOT TRIGGERED (gap 0.304 < 0.326) confirms localization is not the bottleneck, which explains why de-emphasising the box term keeps helping: it reallocates gradient weight to cls/DFL, where the real headroom is (yellow light AP50-95=0.5232 against AP50=0.9125, D5 gap 0.174 and rising toward its 0.227 threshold). D1/D2 TRIGGERED with plateau at epoch 57/100 indicate wasted schedule length, but epochs are not an exposed knob here. I therefore take one further step down the only productive axis, box 4.0 -> 3.0, changing nothing else so the result remains interpretable against the existing four-point curve. Per-step gains are decaying (+0.0063, +0.0024, +0.0027), so 3.0 is plausibly at or just past the turning point; I avoid going lower because excessive de-weighting of regression would eventually harm the tight-IoU metric that dominates mAP50-95.
